tagline: Power Query pushes transformation steps back to the data source — reducing data transfer and improving refresh speed

slides.title: What Is Query Folding?
slides.body: Query Folding is Power Query's ability to translate M transformation steps into native query language (SQL, OData, etc.) that runs on the data source instead of in Power BI. When folding occurs, the source database filters and transforms data before sending it — Power BI receives a smaller, pre-processed result set. When folding does not occur, Power BI downloads all raw data and transforms it locally, which is slower and uses more memory.
slides.keyPoint: Query folding = let the source do the work. The fewer rows and columns Power BI downloads, the faster and more efficient the refresh.

slides.title: Without Query Folding — Inefficient Path
slides.caption: Power BI downloads 10 million raw rows, then filters in memory
slides.note: Network transfers 10M rows; filter and column removal run locally — slow and resource-intensive.

slides.title: With Query Folding — Efficient Path
slides.caption: Power Query translates the M steps into SQL; the database does the filtering
slides.note: Network transfers only the 450K rows that match. The source database uses its indexes for fast filtering.

slides.title: Steps That Preserve Folding
bullets: Filter rows (e.g., keep rows where Year = 2024) → translated to WHERE clause
Remove columns / choose columns → translated to SELECT list
Group by and aggregate → translated to GROUP BY
Sort rows → translated to ORDER BY
Merge queries (join) — may fold if both sources support it and use the same connection
Add conditional column based on source columns → often translated to CASE WHEN
slides.keyPoint: Standard relational transformations (filter, select, aggregate, sort, join) almost always fold against SQL-based sources.

slides.title: Steps That Break Folding
bullets: Merging with a non-foldable or different-source query — folding stops at the merge
Adding an index column (Table.AddIndexColumn) — no SQL equivalent
Using Table.Buffer() — explicitly forces local evaluation
Complex M expressions not translatable to the source's SQL dialect
Connecting to sources that don't support folding (CSV, Excel, JSON files, some REST APIs)
slides.warning: Once a step breaks folding, ALL subsequent steps in that query also run locally — even steps that would otherwise fold. Place non-foldable steps as late as possible in the query to minimize the impact.
slides.keyPoint: Check folding status by right-clicking a step in the Applied Steps pane — a grayed-out 'View Native Query' option means folding stopped at or before that step.

slides.title: PL-300 Exam — Key Facts
bullets: Query folding applies only to Import mode — DirectQuery sends every visual query directly to the source in real time
The 'View Native Query' option in Power Query Editor shows the SQL being generated — if it is grayed out, folding is not occurring for that step
Incremental refresh REQUIRES query folding on the date/time partition column — if folding is broken, incremental refresh falls back to a full refresh
Reference queries do not fold against the original source — duplicate queries are preferred when folding is important for a subset
Table.Buffer() forces local evaluation of a table, permanently breaking folding for all downstream steps
slides.keyPoint: Incremental refresh dependency on query folding is a high-frequency PL-300 exam topic. If incremental refresh is not reducing refresh time, check whether the date column step is still folding.
